notes:
Summary: enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity & traffic shaping. Customer runs latency-sensitive chat for claims triage (support agents + automated triage) plus large nightly embedding job to reindex new docs. Key ask: guaranteed throughput for batch indexing windows and hard low-latency p95 SLOs for chat.

Recent interactions (shorthand):
- 2026-02-12 call (ff-20260212-873): AE/SE + Infra + InfraOps from Boreal. Discussed traffic lanes idea. Boreal: "need fast path for chat, slow/bulk lane for embedding jobs — must not affect chat p95".
- 2026-02-05 email thread: sent initial Dedicated sizing (8xA100 equiv) + price estimate. CFO asking for ARR band justification.
- 2025-11-18 kickoff call (ff-20251118-421): introduced Redwood Dedicated, compliance checklist.
- 2025-12-02 SE deep-dive: provided reference architecture for VPC private deployment and KMS integration.

Technical requirements / constraints (bullet-y):
- Workloads: low-latency chat (p95 target 180ms), throughput ~50 reqs/s peak for chat; nightly bulk embeddings: 120k docs per 4-hr window (~8k/min), batch throughput priority during off-peak only.
- Desired reserved capacity: initial ask 8xA100-class GPUs with burst policy; want ability to scale to 12 GPUs for seasonal peaks.
- Throughput guarantees: committed baseline for embeddings window (sustained tokens/sec or requests/sec) + chat concurrency floors.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 for chat; SLA must include penalty credits if p95 > 250ms for >30min continuous.
- Traffic shaping: per-route quotas (chat route vs embedding route), priority lanes with token-bucket shaping, strict concurrency cap for bulk lane to avoid GPU starvation.
- Noisy-neighbor controls: preemption/fair-share at request level, per-tenant GPU isolation (soft via scheduler + hard via cgroup/containers), KV cache partitioning suggestions.
- Routing/fallbacks: policy to route to compatible lower-cost model variant if dedicated saturated, with automated warm-standby to prevent cold start latency.
- Observability: per-route token/latency breakdowns, trace sampling, and per-tenant GPU utilization dashboards required for SRE review.

POC & benchmarking:
- Running internal benchmark on Redwood test cluster: mixed workload sim showed chat p95 stable under <=60% embedding lane concurrency, but p95 rises after concurrent batch jobs exceed configured throttles. Attach: pocs/boreal-dedicated-benchmark-results.csv.
- Action: need Redwood team to run a controlled noisy-neighbor test with deliberate heavy embedding load to demonstrate mitigations (queueing + lane preemption).

SLA / commercial negotiation notes:
- Boreal wants a two-tier SLA: availability (99.9% monthly) + performance SLOs (chat p95). Legal flagged uptime credits wording; procurement will ask for trial-to-commit conversion terms.
- Pricing sensitivity: CFO comparing Dedicated commit vs cloud on-demand + managed ops. Emphasize unit economics provided by Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Quotes / verbatim snippets from calls: "If chat degrades during indexing we lose SLAs with brokers — cannot accept interruptions"; "We need clear tenant isolation guarantees, not 'best-effort'".

Next immediate steps (short):
- Deliver Dedicated baseline doc with explicit throughput numbers + proposed priority-lane configs (due 2026-03-03).
- Schedule noisy-neighbor test with Redwood infra team by 2026-03-10.
- SE to prepare SLA redline version (Ravi) and share with Legal.
- Procurement cadence: CFO call week of 2026-03-10 to review commitments.

Internal AE notes (tips):
- Emphasize ability to define per-route quotas and automatic fallback models; provide template rate-policy they can copy.
- Show case studies where Dedicated priority lanes prevented production regressions.
- Keep procurement talks focused on predictable cost (reserved GPUs) vs variable op-ex.
